design_notes: S1 modules in scope: M-001 (master CRUD) and M-007 (DB infrastructure). HLD data flows DF-001..DF-005 involve S2+ modules (M-002..M-005) — not yet delivered. S1 cross-module integration is bounded by DF-006 (M-006→M-001 designs/grades contract) and DF-007 (M-007→PostgreSQL alembic+seed). Two additional vertical scenarios exercise the full router→DI→service→repo→DB chain that the per-task tests covered only in isolation.

Container connection refused with `password authentication failed for user 'test'` because the alembic invocation hit the placeholder URL, not the testcontainer's URL.

execution_summary.regression_check: All 8 pre-existing per-task integration tests (TC-018, TC-026, TC-033..TC-038) re-ran and still pass alongside the 4 new IS scenarios. 12/12 integration tests green.

scenarios.name: DF-006: designs API → active grades projection
scenarios.description: End-to-end DF-006 contract that S2 transaction forms depend on. Seeds design + 2 grades + 2 mappings via the HTTP API; deactivates one mapping; GET /designs/{id}/grades returns only the active projection [{grade_id, grade_code}]. Exercises: M-001 schemas, design_service, grade_service, design_grade_map_service, dependencies, all 3 relevant routers, error handlers, M-007 session + repos + ORM. Same chain S2 will consume on every transaction form load.
flow: Caller POSTs design (16X10 / 16X10 Ridges) → 201
Caller POSTs two grades ('1' and 'OB') → both 201
Caller POSTs two mappings (design_id, 1) and (design_id, 2) → both 201
Caller DELETEs the second mapping → 200, is_active=false
Caller GETs /api/v1/designs/{design_id}/grades → 200 with [{grade_id, grade_code}] for the active mapping only
scenarios.entry_point: FastAPI TestClient — POST /api/v1/designs, POST /api/v1/grades, POST /api/v1/design-grade-map, DELETE /api/v1/design-grade-map/{id}, GET /api/v1/designs/{id}/grades
scenarios.exit_assertion: GET response is exactly [{grade_id: <active>, grade_code: '1'}] — no extra fields, only the still-active mapping projected.

scenarios.name: DF-007: alembic migration + seed script → PostgreSQL with 33 master rows
scenarios.description: End-to-end DF-007: brings up a clean PostgreSQL container, applies alembic migration 0002_master_tables (T-024), then runs scripts.seed_master_data.main against it. Verifies that (a) the hand-authored migration applies cleanly to a real PG (closes the W5 verification gap), (b) the migration's schema matches what seed_master_data expects, (c) 33 rows are inserted (3+9+3+9+3+6) matching the PRD samples, (d) re-running the seed inserts 0 new rows (idempotency). This is the only integration scenario that exercises alembic; the per-task tests use Base.metadata.create_all.
flow: Spin up an isolated PostgreSQL 16 testcontainer (separate from the conftest's shared one)
Run `alembic upgrade head` against it — applies migration 0002
Verify all 6 master tables exist with the expected constraint names (uq_grade_master_grade_code, uq_design_grade_map_design_grade)
Invoke scripts.seed_master_data.main() pointed at the container's URL
Assert 3 suppliers + 9 staff + 3 dealers + 9 grades + 3 designs + 6 mappings = 33 rows total
Invoke seed again → 0 new rows (idempotency)
scenarios.exit_assertion: After two seed runs, exactly 33 rows exist across the 6 master tables with the PRD-sample content; both UNIQUE constraints are present in the schema.

scenarios.name: Supplier CRUD lifecycle: router → DI → service → repo → DB → response shape
scenarios.description: Exercises the full M-001 vertical for the supplier entity end-to-end via the HTTP API. Per-task tests (TC-001..TC-006, TC-033..TC-034) cover each layer in isolation; this scenario chains them: POST → GET (default) → PATCH → DELETE → GET (default) → GET (include_inactive=true). Confirms the chain integrates correctly: schemas validate at the boundary, service commits, repo flushes, soft-delete preserves the row, list filters honor include_inactive. Same pattern S2 will follow for transactions.
flow: POST /api/v1/suppliers (Antony Tiles / Kerala) → 201, capture supplier_id
GET /api/v1/suppliers → list contains the new row, is_active=true
PATCH /api/v1/suppliers/{id} (place='Trivandrum') → 200, place updated
DELETE /api/v1/suppliers/{id} → 200, is_active=false
GET /api/v1/suppliers (default) → list does NOT contain the row
GET /api/v1/suppliers?include_inactive=true → list DOES contain the row, is_active=false, place='Trivandrum'
scenarios.exit_assertion: After the round-trip, the row is physically present with is_active=false and the updated place; default list omits it and admin list includes it.

scenarios.name: Cross-feature AC-012 → AC-019: grade deactivation cascades to designs/{id}/grades projection
scenarios.description: When a Grade is deactivated, the M-001 contract GET /designs/{id}/grades must omit any mapping whose grade is now inactive — even if the mapping row itself is still is_active=true. This is the AC-012 → AC-019 cross-feature requirement that the repo's JOIN filter (T-006 list_active_by_design filters BOTH map.is_active AND grade.is_active) enforces. Per-task TC-019 covers this at the service layer; this scenario verifies it end-to-end through the HTTP API after writes go through services + commit.
flow: POST design (12X8 / 12X8 Ridges) → 201, capture design_id
POST grades '1' and '2' → both 201
POST mapping (design, '1') and (design, '2') → both 201 (both is_active=true)
GET /api/v1/designs/{design_id}/grades → 200, body has 2 entries
DELETE /api/v1/grades/{grade_id of '2'} → 200, is_active=false
GET /api/v1/designs/{design_id}/grades → 200, body has ONLY grade '1' — grade '2's mapping is filtered out by the JOIN even though the map row is still active
scenarios.exit_assertion: Final GET body is exactly [{grade_id: <grade1>, grade_code: '1'}]; the (design, grade2) mapping row in tbl_design_grade_map still has is_active=true (only the grade was deactivated, not the mapping).
